Opens the graphics window and has to be called before any drawing command. Calling it again closes the window and opens a new one, and then all images and textures are gone, so load them again. It also puts the colors and the current buffer back to their defaults.

```blitzbasic
;media still display/graphics.png
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
Cls
Text 160, 100, "Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2", 1, 1
Text 160, 120, "Width " + GraphicsWidth() + ", Height " + GraphicsHeight(), 1, 1
Flip
WaitKey
```

![Graphics](media/display/graphics.png)
@param width   Width of the picture in pixels.
@param height  Height of the picture in pixels.
@param depth   Color depth in bits: 0, 16, 24 or 32. Defaults to 0, which lets the system choose.
@param mode    0 opens a window, 1 uses full screen (a borderless window over the display, see [Fullscreen](Fullscreen)), 2 opens a window and 3 opens a window that the user can resize. 4 opens a window without a border: no title bar and no frame. Mode 4 is a BlitzLLVM extension that original Blitz does not have. Defaults to 0.
@gap The color depth is accepted but ignored: the picture always has at least 8 bits each of red, green and blue (with 8 bits of alpha where it is used), because palette and 16 bit rendering are not supported. [GraphicsDepth](GraphicsDepth) says 32 whatever you ask for.
@gap Full screen (mode 1) does not change the video mode of the display: the picture is shown at the largest size that fits with its aspect ratio kept, and the rest is black. See [Fullscreen](Fullscreen).
@gap In a resizable window (mode 3) the picture is scaled to the size of the window, and the mouse position is converted to picture pixels.
@gap The modes 6 and 7 of Blitz3D, which pause the program while the window is in the background, act like 2 and 3. The program keeps running.
@gap In a window without a border (mode 4) the color depth is not used either, and the window has the size you ask for and cannot be resized by the user.
@gap A width or height below 1 stops the program with an error message.
